# ARC-AGI-3 Milestone 2 Solution with a new slot priority (D')

This notebook is [Daniel Franzen's Milestone 2 solution](https://www.kaggle.com/code/dfranzen/arc-agi-3-milestone-2-solution) with one change: **the priority his scheduler uses to decide which game gets an LLM slot.** The harness patch, model, inference engine and prompts are his, unchanged. All credit for them goes to him and to the people he credits below.

**Where this comes from.** D' grew out of the scheduler in our earlier public notebook, [Duck plus ours](https://www.kaggle.com/code/shiiin9/affectify-arc-duck-plus-ours). The idea is the same: rather than give every game an equal share of the thinking time, give it to the games where it is most likely to earn points. That notebook did this with a lottery on top of the Duck harness. Here it is a priority formula on top of Daniel Franzen's scheduler.

| Notebook | Public scores of the same code |
|---|---|
| Daniel Franzen's original | 27.89 (his leaderboard score), 31.47 (best score shown on his notebook page), 27.62 (our unchanged resubmission) |
| This notebook (D') | 31.54 (one submission) |

The same code scores quite differently from run to run: 27.62 to 31.47 for his notebook. One submission of D' is not enough to say by how much it is better. Note that the score at the top of a notebook page is the best of all submissions made from that notebook version, so it shows the luckiest run.

## What changed

1. **A new priority formula.** His scheduler runs 10 games at a time. A running game keeps its slot until its context is trimmed. At each trim it hands the slot back, and the waiting game with the highest priority takes it. We replace that priority (below).
2. **Unstarted games no longer jump the queue.** They are priced by the same formula, so a fresh game competes with games already in progress.

The change lives in the cell just before `await bm.run(...)`. It embeds our module as a string (its comments are in Japanese) and patches his scheduler. It prints `#OURS_FORM ok version=d_prime ...` once the patch is in place, and raises an error if his scheduler's names have changed. The cell right after the run prints how many unstarted games were queued by the formula.

## D': slot priority

**priority = A · M · C + B · φ**

- **A**, depth and action efficiency: (1 + 0.5 (ℓ − 1)) · norm(N) · (300 / (300 + a))^2.5, where norm(N) = 55 / (N (N + 1) / 2) with N clamped to 6..10, as in his code
- **M**, pace: clip((30,000 / p)^0.4, 0.25, 4), where p is the mean tokens per level cleared so far in this game (M = 1 before the first clear)
- **C**, patience: 0.1 · max(0.1, 1 − a / 115) + 0.9 · max(0.1, 1 − t / T), where T = 225,000 · clip(p / 30,000, 0.5, 2)^0.5, so games that needed more tokens per level get more patience
- **B**, room to grow: 16, 14, 10 or 0 when 3 or more, 2, 1 or 0 levels remain
- **φ**, his tail fade: 1 → 0 over the last 40% of the run, so the room-to-grow bonus B fades out near the end

ℓ is the current level (from 1), N the game's level count, and a and t the actions and generated tokens spent on the current level.

How we arrived at this formula and its coefficients is something we are keeping to ourselves for now.

## Save run

To save GPU quota, the save run plays one demo game (ft09) for 5 minutes. It only proves that the notebook runs end to end. The competition rerun (`TRUE_SUBMISSION`) uses his settings unchanged. To run his 10-game demo instead, copy the `demo_excluded_games` line and the second `max_runtime_s_per_game` line of the config cell back from his notebook.

Below is Daniel Franzen's original description.

# About this notebook

This notebook contains my solution for **ARC Prize 2026 — ARC-AGI-3, Milestone 2**, built on [Tufa Labs’ Duck harness](https://www.kaggle.com/code/jeroencottaar/tufa-labs-duck-harness-june-30-milestone-winner). Full credit goes to Jeroen Cottaar and Tufa Labs for the original Duck solver, harness, and notebook.

The attached source bundle is an unchanged copy of Tufa Labs’ original bundle. **All my modifications to the harness are included in the patch at the beginning of this notebook**, which is applied automatically during setup. The patch is based on the original [Duck harness](https://github.com/Tufalabs/duck-harness) at commit `7652836`.

I also switched to [Qwen3.8-Flash-Next](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next), using [Intel’s AutoRound quantization](https://huggingface.co/Intel/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-W4A16-AutoRound) and a separate quantized [MTP draft checkpoint](https://huggingface.co/albucino/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-W4A16-FP8PLE) provided by Albucino for speculative decoding. Inference runs through [Pennyroyal, John Pezzulli’s SGLang fork](https://github.com/jpezzulli/sglang-rtxpro6000), v2.5.3, based on commit [`d00d88e`](https://github.com/jpezzulli/sglang-rtxpro6000/commit/d00d88efc8d6281b12be4f4073126aec95038c55), with contributions and patches from [Mamy Ratsimbazafy](https://github.com/mratsim/sglang-qwen38fn-sm120-turbo) and [Gabriel Olympie](https://github.com/gabrielolympie/sglang-flashnext-sm120), plus my own additional patches.

Third-party code and model weights remain subject to their respective licenses.

**Running your own copy:** After copying this notebook, manually select the **RTX PRO 6000** GPU before running it. Keep all attached source, wheelhouse, and model inputs enabled.

For more information, see my [GitHub repository](https://github.com/da-fr/arc-agi-3-solution).

## 0. Harness patch

Patch to add our modifications to the original tufa harness.

## 1. Environment and submission mode

Detect whether this is a real competition rerun (which minimises diagnostics), set the
framework's environment flags, and put the CUDA libraries on the linker path.

## 2. Precaching

Precache wheelhouse for faster startup.

## 3. Install the ARC runtime

Install `arc-agi` from the offline competition wheelhouse (the Kaggle submission environment
has no internet).

## 4. Import the bundled source

Put the snapshotted repositories on the path (this process and any child processes).

## 5. Start serving

Install and startup sglang to serve the model.

## 6. Load the benchmark

Unpickle the deployment target and the benchmark, stamping the real submission state onto the
target and pointing the benchmark's outputs at the Kaggle working directory.

## 7. Customization hook

Optional: tweak `bm`, `bm.games`, or `bm.solver` here before the run starts — the safe place
for one-off experiments once the deployed bundle has loaded.

## 8. Run the system monitor

Periodically show free main memory, VRAM and disk space.

## 9. Run the benchmark

In a real competition rerun (`KAGGLE_IS_COMPETITION_RERUN`), wait for the Kaggle gateway and
play the **live competition Arcade**. Otherwise — an interactive "Save & Run" — play the
competition's **bundled environment files offline**, with no gateway required, so the notebook
runs end-to-end without a submission. Teardown commands run afterward even if the run raises.

## 10. Show the diagnostics

A non-submission run writes `diagnostics.html` to `/kaggle/working`; it is rendered inline below
(and downloadable from the working directory). You should be able to click around through the links.
